author: nicolas
summary: Grammar rulings G24–G31 from the open-questions review of 2026-10-17 (ADR-0012), and the three examples ADR-0011 left to revise. 1.1 stays vocabulary-only (ADR-0009); these land on top of it.

rulings.ruling: A time word or time correlative (eli-krono, deyapressa, fututi, ki-krono's answers…) may open its clause or close it. When it opens the clause, the comma after it is optional. Only the four frame words zafra, finra, lanto and kenvi are opening-only, and they keep their comma.

A single oro joins two equal constituents, exactly as ata does: miru oro nami, water or food. It may also open a clause or line that continues the one before ("Or …"). The pair oro A oro B is the emphatic "either A or B".
examples: oro maivo ke li suma ki?

rulings.topic: Give-type verbs: where the recipient goes
rulings.ruling: A verb of giving (give, lend, send, owe, sell, pay, bring, teach, show) takes VERB THEME ala RECIPIENT. When the recipient is a pronoun it may instead stand bare straight after the verb: VERB PRONOUN THEME. Any other recipient takes ala.
examples: Fisa, rimara tressa cono ala maivo.

rulings.topic: Which side of de is the owner
rulings.ruling: In X de Y the owner is Y, read as English "X of Y": li bumre de li cilni, the bread of the city; li lira de amor, the song of love. One exception: a pronoun or a personal name (pilo, father, used as a name included) standing before de is the owner, read as English "X's Y": maivo de lira, my song; pilo de bumre, father's bread. A pronoun is the owner wherever it stands: li purma de maivo, my parent. Fractions (tressa de cuara) are their own construction.
examples: Li bitiri de pilo ka su li tabu.
Father's tools are on the table.
Eli bumre ka sambasan ko pilo de bumre.
This bread is the same as father's bread.
Li bumre de li cilni ka sambanasan da eli bumre.
City bread is different from this bread.
Nullo de deyaapo, maivo po ne somusia.

rulings.ruling: After a number or a quantifier the plural -ri is optional: the number already says how many. Choose by sound and meter. Without a number or quantifier, a plural noun takes -ri.
examples: Maivo po vimova muya jemlari en li folni.
I saw many insects on the flower.

rulings.topic: An adjective standing as a noun
rulings.ruling: An adjective may stand as a noun phrase on its own only after an article or determiner (li, eli, ola, baba): li ramumomvisan, the forgotten. Without one, an adjective needs its noun.
examples: yesta li raleri de li sadori de li ramumomvisan po lenila maivori de lira.
even the echoes of the sorrows of the forgotten heard our song

rulings.ruling: Liraasa has no word for "about / concerning". A song, story or word about something is a de phrase under G27: li lira de amor, the song of (about) love. After a verb of saying, give the verb an object rather than su: po sarbisia lirari de amor, wrote songs of love.
examples: Li ralelirapatu de li lira ka melosan.
Li veluri po sarbisia lirari de amor.
The stars wrote songs of love.

rulings.ruling: A command has no subject: the clause opens at the verb (slot 3 notes), softened with fisa. A person addressed is a noun phrase set off by commas, at the start or end of the clause. In verse, once the time has been set, the bare present may narrate past events.
examples: Taivo viki pagopa ligo maivo ki, maivo de amor?
Would you come near me, my love?

ops.to: Time words open or close a clause; the opening comma is optional; zafra, finra, lanto, kenvi stay opening-only.
ops.reason: Canon closes clauses with eli-krono (Saivo po venreva pendi eli-krono; Li navutrana ne ka sovesan eli-krono) and once omits the comma (Eli-krono maivo lirala). Author's ruling, 2026-10-17.
ops.author: nicolas

ops.to: A lone oro joins two equal parts like ata, and may open a continuing clause; oro A oro B is emphatic either/or.
ops.reason: The function-word table's own example is a lone oro (miru oro nami). Author's ruling, 2026-10-17.
ops.author: nicolas

ops.to: A give-type verb takes THEME ala RECIPIENT, or a bare pronoun recipient straight after the verb.
ops.reason: Canon writes guraga maivo (pendi) (dossa) cono four times; every bare recipient in canon is a pronoun. Author's ruling, 2026-10-17.
ops.author: nicolas

ops.to: In X de Y the owner is Y, except a pronoun or personal name before de is the owner; a pronoun is always the owner.
ops.reason: Fits every one of the 65 canon de phrases, including pilo de bumre, livna de taivo and nullo de deyaapo. Author's ruling, 2026-10-17.
ops.author: nicolas

ops.to: -ri is optional after a number or quantifier.
ops.reason: Canon has both dossa veluri and dossa cono, muya jemlari and muya marna. Author's ruling, 2026-10-17.
ops.author: nicolas

ops.to: An adjective stands as a noun only after an article or determiner.
ops.reason: li ramumomvisan, "the forgotten", in Lira de Kronoasa; the -san ending keeps it parseable. Author's ruling, 2026-10-17.
ops.author: nicolas

ops.to: "About" is a de phrase; no new word.
ops.reason: 1.0 has no word for about; a de phrase is short, singable and reads as English verse (songs of love). Author's ruling, 2026-10-17.
ops.author: nicolas

ops.to: Commands have no subject (fisa softens); address is set off by commas; verse may narrate in the present.
ops.reason: Commands and address are already written this way in canon (Vulravelmava maivo de yendo, fisa; …ki, maivo de amor?); the narrative present gives verse metrical freedom. Author's ruling, 2026-10-17.
ops.author: nicolas

ops.to: Maivo de benasan melo opioa lumi.
ops.reason: ADR-0011: melo bena is noun + noun, melo sat in the verb slot, and the pronoun owner lacked de. Rewritten to keep the gloss "My good music hopes for light" using only existing forms.
ops.author: nicolas

ops.from: Lotero silda, li cilni ka lasona.
ops.to: Loterosan silda, li cilni ka lasona.
ops.reason: ADR-0011: lotero silda is noun + noun; loterosan is the adjective "other".
ops.author: nicolas

ops.from: Maivo po lemula baba lotero lermi.
ops.to: Maivo po lemula baba loterosan lermi.
ops.reason: ADR-0011: lotero lermi is noun + noun; loterosan is the adjective "other".
